Ultimately murder is not wrong. The deer has no right to life when confronted with the lion. The chicken has no right to life when confronted with us. That is natural law and this is the system that creates the strongest lions and the most cunning deer. That being said, I am a libertarian and so I believe in contracts and I believe in personal preferences. If people want to get together and agree to live under the contract of the non-aggression principle, then we can agree to draw our lines of personal behaviour at where they infringe on the rights of another person. This is not a system based on moral truths or objective facts, it is just an agreement of personal preferences. With that understanding, we can say that murder is illegal because it infringes on the individual liberty of the victim. This is an effective system for a peaceful, non-chaotic society. However, from a purely moral standpoint, there is no such thing as wrong. The closest you can come is to have several people all agree that their personal preference is not to be murdered. Even a perfect consensus, however, doesn't establish objective truth or moral reality because everyone can theoretically agree to something that is false.
